key_insight: Within physics-informed learning, B-spline representations can be compared fairly with neural networks and may offer better-behaved training and accuracy under the same PDE-solving framework.
engineering_relevance: For PDE-based modeling, inverse design, and parametric simulation, the choice of representation can materially affect convergence speed, robustness, and required numerical precision.
method: Compare neural networks and B-splines in a common physics-informed learning setup
Test both representations on four PDE problems with closed-form solutions
Analyze asymptotic convergence, sampling needs, loss minimization, and arithmetic precision
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a numerical study on four closed-form benchmark problems to evaluate accuracy and efficiency across the two representations.
watch_item: Results may depend on the selected benchmark PDEs and training setup, so performance gains should be validated on the target application before adoption.
paper_title: Comparison of neural and spline representations for physics-informed learning
